blk_part_01_part_1_a_model_is_not_the_sa.text: AI news often treats models, chatbots, and agents as if they were identical. A large language model, or LLM, produces and interprets language. An agent uses a model as part of a larger system that can take actions. To examine such systems, we can use three questions: What model supports the system? What tools can it use? When must a human intervene?

blk_part_01_part_1_a_model_is_not_the_sa.text: Grok Bot, introduced in early beta on 11 August 2026, is a team of always-on agents. Each agent has its own cloud computer and can sign into tools and apps. It can work across websites, including sites without an API—a formal connection that allows software systems to communicate directly. The agents are intended to complete jobs from beginning to end and return to the user when approval is needed.

blk_part_03_part_3_what_anthropic_means_.text: Researchers call this internal structure J-space because they study it with a Jacobian lens, or J-lens. In simplified terms, the lens connects patterns in the model’s neural activations with verbal concepts. Neural activations are changing numerical states inside the model as it processes information. They are different from a visible chain-of-thought scratchpad, which consists of generated text. J-space exists in the activations themselves.

Grok 4.6 concerns model capability, particularly long-running and interactive work. Grok Bot adds tools and a working environment, allowing agents to act across websites and return when approval is required. J-space research addresses a different problem: whether researchers can gain limited visibility into internal patterns that may not appear in a model’s output.

blk_part_05_part_5_comparing_capability_.text: A careful evaluation therefore combines practical and scientific evidence. For an agent, we might ask what it can access, what actions require approval, and how errors are handled. For an LLM, we might examine its behavior while also studying internal representations through methods such as the J-lens. New AI systems may become more capable while remaining only partly interpretable, which makes precise language and realistic limits especially important.
